visible_observation: The headline 'WHERE THE HOUSES END' is set in a uniform, wide-tracking serif font that floats centrally in the negative space, completely detached from the visual elements. The tagline 'Some places disappear twice' is rendered in a standard italic serif that lacks visual distinction from the main title.
critique: The typography fails to embody the film's themes of memory and erasure. The headline is static and legible, acting as a label rather than a visual participant in the composition. It ignores the 'fading' motif present in the imagery (the ghost house) and sits too cleanly on top of the scene, breaking the atmospheric immersion. The text does not interact with the vanishing point of the road.
revision: Apply a vertical SVG mask or gradient to the headline so the text fades into transparency at the edges, mimicking the 'disappearing' houses. Shift the tagline to a smaller, widely tracked sans-serif or a distressed serif to differentiate the hierarchy and suggest the fragility of memory.
protected_strength: The atmospheric, low-contrast color palette and the geometric perspective of the road leading into the fog.
